title: One-on-one evals playbook + prep notes — Rajiv Mar16
content:
Quick TL;DR:
- Prep for 1:1 with Sofia (optimize lead) — focus on two recent regressions in chat-quality A/B and the tiny-embedding rerank test.
- Goal: agree immediate mitigation (hotfix prompt tweaks + fallback routing) and a 2-week follow-up experiment plan.

Agenda (30–40m):
1) 5m - What changed since last sync (deploys, model pins, infra)
2) 10m - Walk through top 3 regression signals and concrete examples
3) 10m - Discuss A/B split (traffic, gating, early metrics) + decide rollback or fix-in-place
4) 5–10m - Actions, owners, and quick experiments to run this week

Important context notes (notes to self, unpolished):
- Two regressions surfaced in last night’s alert bundle (03-15):
  * chat-quality: automated eval metric (BLEU-for-clauses) down ~5.4% for the customer-support prompt set (heavy in follow-ups).
  * rerank-embeds: MRR drop 0.08 on tiny-embedding A/B across two queries (likely quantization subtlety).
- Both pipelines were touched by the batcher change (optimize/batching PR #412) + kernel update on dedicated nodes (driver 2.9). Need to confirm ordering.
- Slack thread: #evals-alerts (link pinned in confluence) — there are raw examples and user complaints snippets.

Concrete examples to show in 1:1 (copy-paste):
- Prompt ID: cs-support-2026-03-08-v2
  input: "Customer: I changed my billing address but my invoice shows old address."
  expected (gold): "I'm sorry about that — I can update your billing address. Can you confirm the last 4 of the card used?"
  current output: "You need to update billing in settings. Go to billing settings."
  failure mode: hallucinated instruction, skipped empathic opener, lost context of previous message.

- Rerank case: query "site:docs how to rehydrate cache" — baseline ranks KB article A above B; new ranks swap A/B causing user confusion (tracked by click-through delta).

Immediate hypotheses (brainstorm):
- batching PR caused slight prefix-cutoff in KV cache, leading to missing context for long multi-turn prompts.
- kernel update modified softmax numerics (rare), causing embedding quant rounding that moves some vectors across decision boundary.
- prompt-template rendering: a whitespace trimming bug for follow-up messages introduced last week.

Quick experiments I want to propose (cheap, <24h):
1) Canary revert: route 10% traffic back to previous batching kernel for 3 hours and compare chat-quality metric for same prompt bucket. (Owner: Sofia)
2) Prompt hotfix: apply quick guard (add explicit 'include prior message history' clause) to cs-support prompt and run isolated evals on 500 seed cases. If improvement > 3% then rollout. (Owner: Rajiv)
3) Embedding QA: re-run quantization sweep on the tiny-embedding model for the top 200 failure queries with high-margin vectors to inspect distance shifts. (Owner: Liam)
4) Create per-customer diff snapshots for last 24h affected requests for audit + SRE (Owner: Rajiv + SRE oncall).

Metrics dashboard pointers (what to open in meeting):
- evals/ui/chat-quality -> filter by prompt-tag: cs-support-2026
- optimize/ab-tests -> A/B group splits + user-level CTR; export last 48h
- infra/traces -> batcher-latency map for last deploy window

Open questions to raise (need decisions):
- Triage policy: do we rollback A/B or fix-in-place? if fix-in-place, what guard thresholds?
- SLA impact: are any enterprise customers hitting increased error/latency? (if so, escalate to CS)
- Visibility: should we add a regression alert threshold for MRR drops >0.05 to trigger paging?

Action items (post-meeting, assign here so I don't forget):
- [ ] Rajiv: run prompt-hotfix isolated eval and post results to thread (#evals-hotfix) by EOD. (priority: high)
- [ ] Sofia: schedule 10% canary revert and monitor chat-quality metric; report within 4h of start. (priority: high)
- [ ] Liam: start quant-sweep and upload diffs for top 50 vectors; note any >0.02 cosine shifts. (priority: medium)
- [ ] Rajiv + SRE: collect request-level logs + KV cache traces for two failing examples and put in confluence page. (priority: high)
- [ ] Rajiv: draft short FYI for CS if rollback may affect feature flags (priority: medium)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep examples short in meeting — show 2 good vs 2 bad. People glaze over long trace dumps.
- If Sofia pushes rollback, ask for exact gating metrics and rollback playbook steps.
- Don't promise customers anything until we confirm root cause + mitigation path.

Follow-up timeline:
- Today: hotfix eval + canary + quant-sweep kicked off.
- 48h: decision window for rollback vs fix-in-place based on canary data.
- 2 weeks: larger A/B or model retrain if root cause tied to quantization or model drift.

Random thoughts / future experiments (parking lot):
- Add a lightweight synthetic test that simulates multi-turn follow-ups to catch prefix-trimming regressions automatically.
- For embeddings, add check that nearest-neighbor rank stability > 0.95 after any quant/change.

End of scratchpad.
(Will tidy into a confluence post if Sofia asks for a single-source post-mortem.)
